chunks: 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from some of his companions, from al-Washsha', from Abi Khaythamah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

"Indeed, my father instructed me to wash him when he passed away, and he said to me: 'Write, my son.' Then he said: 'They will command you to do contrary to what you are doing, so say to them: This is my father's written instruction, and I do not go beyond his word.' Then he said: 'You begin by washing his hands, then perform wudu (ablution) for him as the wudu of salat (prayer), then take water and lote leaves.'"
The rest of the hadith follows, and what he mentioned of the du'a (supplication) at the time of washing the deceased.

key_terms.أَغْسِلَهُ: to perform ghusl for him, meaning to wash the deceased
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), used here to specify the form of wudu
key_terms.سِدْرًا: lote leaves mixed with water in the washing of the deceased
key_terms.مَاءً: water used for the ritual washing
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution) performed in the manner of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the proper method of washing the deceased in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration describes instructions for the ghusl of the deceased, transmitted from a father to his son with emphasis on adhering to the written directive. It outlines the opening steps of the ritual washing, including washing the hands, performing wudu (ablution) for the deceased, and preparing water with sidr, while also indicating that supplications are recited during the process.
